I reproduced this standalone in Node (isolating just the comparator, both old and new construction) across the same 6 permutations the smoke uses: OLD construction yields exactly 3 distinct final orders (a-small,m-nan,z-big then z-big,a-small,m-nan then m-nan,z-big,a-small), matching F-005's repro claim verbatim, and the pinned expected order z-big,a-small,m-nan only coincidentally matches 2 of the 6 old permutations (index-orders 0,2,1 and 1,2,0) -- so the new assertion would genuinely fail on 4 of 6 permutations (0,1,2 / 1,0,2 / 2,0,1 / 2,1,0) under the old code. NEW construction (NaN normalized to null before the sort) collapses all 6 permutations to the single order z-big,a-small,m-nan, and the nan burnInputTokens===null assertion also only holds post-fix (old code left it as NaN, not null). Conclusion: the permutation assertion genuinely pins the fixed contract against CHK-001:happy:6 (deterministic order regardless of input row order) and CHK-001:adversarial:4 (NaN rows never corrupt findings) -- not a coincidental/weak pin.
